title: Methemoglobin determination by multi-component analysis in coho salmon (Oncorhynchus kisutch) possessing unstable hemoglobin
author: Blair, Barlow, et al.
materials: In order to determine the molar absorptivities of coho hemoglobin derivatives, four hemoglobin stock solutions were prepared within 2–3 h after blood collection from the Quilcene hatchery following Riggs [5]. Red blood cells were pelleted by centrifugation (800 x g, 10 min, 4 °C), triple washed in ice cold 0.96% NaCl (aq) and resuspended to their original hematocrit in 20 mM phosphate buffered saline (PBS) at pH 8.0, and to 330 mOsm/kg using NaCl to approximate adult coho plasma osmolality [6]. Red cells were lysed by addition of phosphate-buffered 0.5% Triton X-100 and cellular debris was removed by centrifugation (10,000 x g, 12 min, 4 °C), before passing hemolysates through a 0.45 μm pore size polyethersulfone (PES) syringe filter. Coho hemoglobin stock solutions were stored at 4 °C for no longer than 4 days. Oxyhemoglobin and carboxyhemoglobin measurements were performed immediately following hemoglobin stock preparations to prevent autoxidation during storage time. Storage time of hemoglobin stocks did not affect measurements for the remaining hemoglobin derivatives.

steps.title: Prepare hemoglobin stock solutions
steps.instruction: Collect coho salmon blood and, within 2–3 h, pellet red blood cells by centrifugation at 800 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; triple‑wash the pellet in ice‑cold 0.96 % NaCl (aq); resuspend to the original hematocrit in 20 mM phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) pH 8.0 adjusted to 330 mOsm kg⁻¹ with NaCl; lyse cells by adding phosphate‑buffered 0.5 % Triton X‑100; remove debris by centrifugation at 10 000 × g for 12 min at 4 °C; filter the hemolysate through a 0.45 µm polyethersulfone (PES) syringe filter; store the hemoglobin stock at 4 °C for no more than 4 days; measure oxy‑ and carboxyhemoglobin immediately after preparation to avoid autoxidation (storage does not affect other derivatives).

steps.title: Generate oxy‑, carboxy‑, and deoxyhemoglobin
steps.instruction: From the fresh stock, obtain oxyhemoglobin by exposing the solution to ambient O₂; confirm absence of a ~630 nm methemoglobin peak; then incubate the same sample under humidified CO gas for 15 min to convert to carboxyhemoglobin and record its spectrum; prepare deoxyhemoglobin by placing stock on ice under humidified N₂ gas and incubating until a single stable absorption peak appears (3–4 h), using N₂ that has been bubbled through a vanadous chloride solution to remove residual O₂.

steps.title: Prepare hemichrome derivative
steps.instruction: Dilute the hemoglobin stock in PBS containing 0.5 M sodium salicylate; add a slight molar excess of potassium ferricyanide; allow conversion, which is nearly complete in 45 min and proceeds slowly up to ~4 h until the spectral pattern stabilises.

steps.title: Create duplicate derivative samples
steps.instruction: For each of the four independent hemoglobin stock solutions, prepare duplicate aliquots of oxyhemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, deoxyhemoglobin, and hemichrome.

steps.title: Prepare 100 % methemoglobin stock
steps.instruction: Add an 18‑fold molar excess of sodium nitrite to a hemoglobin stock to fully oxidise it to methemoglobin; avoid potassium ferricyanide to minimise ICP‑MS iron‑content errors.

steps.title: Dialyze and filter methemoglobin stock
steps.instruction: Inject the methemoglobin solution into a 10 mL Pierce™ Slide‑A‑Lyzer cassette and dialyse against 1 L 20 mM PBS, performing four buffer exchanges; centrifuge the dialysate at 10 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C and filter through a 0.45 µm PES syringe filter; note that the resulting stock may contain both methemoglobin and hemichrome but did not form hemichrome in this preparation.

steps.title: Prepare methemoglobin for absorptivity range
steps.instruction: Using the methemoglobin stock, prepare assay solutions at pH 7.8, 7.6, 7.4, 7.2, and 6.8 by diluting in 20 mM PBS adjusted to 330 mOsm L⁻¹ with NaCl, following the same procedure as for other derivatives.

steps.title: Collect spectral time series after ferricyanide
steps.instruction: Add a slight excess of potassium ferricyanide to a hemoglobin solution; record absorbance spectra continuously for ~18 min, noting rapid conversion to methemoglobin within 1 min followed by conversion to hemichrome over ~15 min and eventual precipitation (baseline rise, loss of isosbestic points).

steps.title: Iterative MATLAB modeling of metHb → hemichrome
steps.instruction: In MATLAB R2017a, load the m × n spectral matrix (m = 251 wavelengths 450–700 nm, n = time points); perform singular‑value decomposition and retain the first two eigenvectors to obtain a rank‑reduced matrix \(\bar R = \bar U \bar Σ \bar V^T\); initialise a guess for the pseudo‑first‑order rate constant κ (s⁻¹); compute the rotation matrix \(\hat H = \bar V^T \; C^+\) where C is the concentration matrix derived from the integrated rate law \([A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-κt}\) and \([B]_t = [A]_0 - [A]_t\); iteratively update κ, \(\hat H\), and \(V'^{T}=\hat H C\) using a Simplex optimisation to minimise the difference between \(V'^{T}\) and the measured \(\bar V^{T}\); once optimal κ is found, calculate the reconstructed spectra \(R' = \hat H \; \bar Σ \; \bar U^{T}\).

steps.title: Determine molar absorptivities via MCA
steps.instruction: Using MATLAB, input the full absorbance vector aHb (251 × 1) for a sample and the molar‑absorptivity matrix Mε (251 × 5) for the five derivatives; compute concentrations by least‑squares: CHb = Mε⁺ aHb (Moore‑Penrose pseudoinverse); ensure the model includes all present derivatives—remove absent ones one at a time, recompute, and inspect residual spectra; confirm that final residuals are minimal and all concentrations are non‑negative before accepting results.

steps.title: Validate MCA method with standards
steps.instruction: Prepare five standard mixtures containing 4.7, 7.5, 9.7, 19.7, and 48.8 % methemoglobin by mixing appropriate volumes of 100 % oxyhemoglobin and 100 % methemoglobin stocks; analyse each mixture with the MCA workflow; compare calculated methemoglobin percentages to values verified by ICP‑MS; accept the MCA result if the relative percent difference is ≤5 % of the ICP‑MS value; note that all MCA results met this criterion, whereas the human multi‑wavelength method exceeded it.
